test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 12 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A tap fills a cistern in 9 hours. Another tap empties the full tank in 90 hours. How long (in hours) will it take to fill twice the volume of the tank, if the tank is empty initially and both the taps are open together?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net efficiency = 1/9 − 1/90 = (10 − 1)/90 = 9/90 = 1/10 per hour.

Time to fill one tank = 10 hours.

Time to fill **twice the volume** = 10 × 2 = 20 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Filling tap time = 9 hours, Emptying tap time = 90 hours.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = LCM of time | Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 
 **Person** **Hours** **Total Work** **Efficiency** 
 Filling Tap 9 90 units +10 
 Emptying Tap 90 −1 

⇒ Combined efficiency = 10 − 1 = 9 units/hour

⇒ Capacity of tank = 90 units

⇒ Target volume (twice) = 90 × 2 = 180 units

⇒ Time required = 180 ÷ 9 = 20 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 20 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inlet and Outlet Taps

Inlet pipes have positive efficiency as they add water, while outlet/leakage pipes have negative efficiency as they remove water.

Net Work Done

If two pipes fill and empty at rates 'a' and 'b', the net rate is (1/a − 1/b) per unit time.

Volume Scaling

If the volume to be filled is multiplied by a factor 'k', the total time taken also scales by 'k' assuming constant rates.</p
